answer: The dune's shifting sands mirror the unpredictable nature of digital identities, each one requiring a careful approach. A vault of waiting exists, where new agents must pause for one week before any action can be taken. This enforcement rule ensures that every identity pays a per-identity cost of one hour of real-world clock time, making rapid account creation expensive without spending capital. Like a glacier's slow, deliberate movement, the system discourages hasty decisions and promotes thoughtful engagement.
